LEADER: George Kurtz, President and CEO, beneficially owned 2,384,082 shares, marked * (less than 1%) against 254,580,533 Class A shares, so pctEconomic is null. The figure includes 1,804,119 shares held of record, 111,099 shares held by trusts with an independent trustee, 16,875 PSU shares vesting within 60 days, 351,989 options exercisable within 60 days and 100,000 shares held by the Kurtz Family Dynasty Trust. In the 2025 proxy he was listed with 6,321,555 shares (2.53%), most of the difference being shares held by trusts with an independent trustee (4,245,383 then, 111,099 now). BUYBACKS: the board authorized a $1.0 billion repurchase program in June 2025, but the fiscal 2026 cash-flow statement shows no repurchases; the 10-K's subsequent-events note reports $50.6 million repurchased between February 1 and March 4, 2026 (fiscal 2027). STOCK COMP: the note total ($1,097.668 million) differs slightly from the cash-flow add-back ($1,096.679 million); the 10-K also corrected an immaterial prior-period error in the timing of stock-based compensation (Note 16).

footprint.notes: CrowdStrike publishes very little about where it operates. The FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended Jan 31, 2026) gives 10,698 full-time employees with no country or state split, describes a deliberately distributed workforce ('the ability to work remotely or in a hybrid arrangement is a deliberate strategy'), and names only its Austin headquarters, adding that it leases offices "in various locations throughout the United States as well as office space in a number of countries in Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific region". The only geographic non-revenue figure is property and equipment plus right-of-use assets, recorded in $ thousands as filed; 'Other countries' ($84,222 thousand) is a residual and is not shown. No state-level figures appear in the 10-K; no company impact report was looked for beyond it.
